questions.q: Where does a parent-to-child subquery go, and where does a semi-join subquery go?
options: Parent-to-child in the SELECT list; semi-join in the WHERE clause
Parent-to-child in the WHERE clause; semi-join in the SELECT list
Both in the FROM clause
Both in the ORDER BY clause
questions.explain: The parent-to-child subquery sits in the SELECT list and returns nested child records. The semi-join sits in WHERE and only filters.

questions.q: What does the inner FROM name in (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) inside an Account query's SELECT list?
options: The child relationship name
The object's API name, Contact
A custom field name
The Account's Id
questions.explain: Parent-to-child subqueries use the child relationship name (plural for standard relationships), not the object name.

questions.q: What does the inner FROM name in WHERE Id IN (SELECT AccountId FROM Opportunity)?
options: The object name, Opportunity
A relationship name ending in __r
The parent Account's name
Nothing; the FROM is optional in a subquery
questions.explain: Semi-join and anti-join subqueries name the real object being filtered against.

questions.q: Which of these does SOQL not support?
options: A subquery in the FROM clause (derived tables)
A subquery in the WHERE clause using IN
A parent-to-child subquery in the SELECT list
Combining a semi-join with a child subquery in one query
questions.explain: SOQL has no derived tables. The outer FROM names a single object. The other three patterns are all supported.

questions.q: In the query that returns Accounts with a Closed Won Opportunity, each with its Contacts, what does the WHERE semi-join decide?
options: Which Accounts appear in the result
Which Contact fields are returned
How the Contacts are sorted
Whether the query counts against governor limits
questions.explain: The semi-join filters the outer Accounts. The SELECT-list subquery separately decides which related Contact data each one carries.
